page: Microsoft Azure L64as_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an x86_64 AMD processor running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 64 dedicated vCPUs and 512 GB of RAM, establishing a memory allocation of 8 GB per vCPU. This ratio accommodates applications that require high concurrent compute capacity alongside sizable working memory sets.

A defining characteristic of this configuration is its bundled local storage subsystem, which features 15,359 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD capacity. The instance also supports Azure Premium Storage for external disk attachments. It does not include hardware GPU acceleration or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, directing its architectural profile entirely toward high-throughput data processing and local disk access.

By delivering over 15 TB of high-speed local NVMe storage coupled with a balanced 1:8 compute-to-memory ratio, the instance eliminates local I/O bottlenecks in dense multi-core scenarios. The hardware distribution provides cost efficiency for environments seeking large ephemeral storage and memory density without provisioning multiple smaller nodes. It is suited for large relational and NoSQL databases, transactional data stores, search indexing engines, and distributed big data analytics.
